Here is a factual research note on the event: “Western Colorado Community Foundation announces $82,000 in grants for 13 conservation projects,” based on original sources and independent confirmation.  

---

## What Actually Happened

**Who made the announcement:**  
The Western Colorado Community Foundation (WCCF) through its CORE (Conservation, Outdoor Recreation, and Environment) Giving Circle. ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai))

**When the grants were awarded:**  
Grants were awarded on **November 6, 2026**. ([gjsentinel.com](https://www.gjsentinel.com/news/western_colorado/wccfs-core-giving-circle-awards-82-500-to-13-outdoor-and-nature-projects/article_63b2fe86-52a9-4b68-ae57-2fb13661b0a0.html?utm_source=openai))

**Amount and scope:**  
- Total of **$82,500** awarded (not $82,000) across **13 separate projects** focused on conservation, outdoor recreation, and environmental education in western Colorado. ([gjsentinel.com](https://www.gjsentinel.com/news/western_colorado/wccfs-core-giving-circle-awards-82-500-to-13-outdoor-and-nature-projects/article_63b2fe86-52a9-4b68-ae57-2fb13661b0a0.html?utm_source=openai))  
- The 2026 grant cycle received **34 applications** requesting over **$266,000** in total. ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai))  

**Categories of work funded:**  
Projects span a range of activities including habitat restoration; wildfire recovery; dust-on-snow and hydroclimate monitoring; outdoor infrastructure upgrades; environmental and outdoor education; river stewardship; student recreation; and community engagement efforts. ([gjsentinel.com](https://www.gjsentinel.com/news/western_colorado/wccfs-core-giving-circle-awards-82-500-to-13-outdoor-and-nature-projects/article_63b2fe86-52a9-4b68-ae57-2fb13661b0a0.html?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Who Received Grants & for What Projects  

The 13 awarded projects are:

| Grantee | Project |
|---|---|
| Aspen Valley Land Trust | Habitat restoration at **Silt River Preserve** ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai)) |
| Center for Snow and Avalanche Studies | **Dust-on-snow and hydroclimate monitoring** ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai)) |
| Colorado Canyons Association | Canyon Club ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai)) |
| Colorado Pheasants and Quail Forever | **Snyder Wildfire Restoration** ([gjsentinel.com](https://www.gjsentinel.com/news/western_colorado/wccfs-core-giving-circle-awards-82-500-to-13-outdoor-and-nature-projects/article_63b2fe86-52a9-4b68-ae57-2fb13661b0a0.html?utm_source=openai)) |
| D51 Foundation | Outdoor Wilderness Lab ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai)) |
| EUREKA! McConnell Science Museum | Environmental & outdoor education for Spanish-speaking families ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai)) |
| National Forest Foundation | Lands End Observatory infrastructure update ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai)) |
| Partners Youth Mentoring (Delta, Montrose & Ouray) | Adventure Partners ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai)) |
| RiversEdge West | River Stewardship and Education Program ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai)) |
| Riverside Education Centers | Seeds to Summits: Planting Opportunities for Outdoor Student RECreation ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai)) |
| Ruth Powell Hutchins Water Center, Colorado Mesa University (CMU) | Colorado Water Fellows Program ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai)) |
| Two Rivers Wildfire Coalition | Neighborhood Ambassador Program ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai)) |
| Western Slope Conservation Center | The Next 25 Years of River Watch ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai)) |

---

## Verification & Source Notes

- **Primary source:** WCCF published a press release titled *“Western Colorado Community Foundation Awards $82,500 Through CORE Giving Circle”* confirming all the details above including the project list, total amount funded, date awarded, and number of applications received. ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Independent media source:** The Grand Junction Daily Sentinel reported on the same topic, confirming the $82,500 total and number of projects, including many of the same grantees. ([gjsentinel.com](https://www.gjsentinel.com/news/western_colorado/wccfs-core-giving-circle-awards-82-500-to-13-outdoor-and-nature-projects/article_63b2fe86-52a9-4b68-ae57-2fb13661b0a0.html?utm_source=openai))  
- **Additional confirmation:** Philanthropy outlets (Wisevoter etc.) reproduced the details. ([wisevoter.com](https://wisevoter.com/world/us/co/2026/11/08/western-colorado-foundation-awards-outdoor-grants?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Completed/Measured Outcomes vs. Announcements

- **Outcome:** The funds have been committed—the grants are awarded and recipients selected. ([wc-cf.org](https://wc-cf.org/2026coregrants/?utm_source=openai))  
- **Not just a pledge or plan:** These are completed grant awards, not just announcements of intention.  
- **What is not yet measurable or detailed:** The timeline and metrics for implementation of each project are not specified in the sources; amounts to individual grantees are typically not disclosed per project. ([wisevoter.com](https://wisevoter.com/world/us/co/2026/11/08/western-colorado-foundation-awards-outdoor-grants?utm_source=openai))  

---

stories.research_notes:
Here is a concise factual research note on the candidate event: **“ICU reassessment links perfusion non-recovery to higher sepsis mortality.”**

---

## What Happened — The Primary Study

A new observational cohort study titled *“Forty-eight-hour coagulation–perfusion recovery as a bedside reassessment framework in critical illness: a multidatabase landmark cohort study”* was published in *Frontiers in Medicine* on 13 November 2026. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2026.1934924/full?utm_source=openai))

### Study Design

- Retrospective “landmark” cohort design using two large public ICU databases: **MIMIC-IV** and **eICU-CRD**. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2026.1934924/full?utm_source=openai))  
- Included adult patients with sepsis who survived at least 48 hours in the ICU. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2026.1934924/full?utm_source=openai))  
- Defined two physiological domains of recovery by 48 hours after ICU admission:
  1. **Coagulation recovery**: assessed via platelet count and international normalized ratio (INR) changes or normalization.  
  2. **Perfusion recovery**: primarily via lactate clearance or normalization. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2026.1934924/full?utm_source=openai))  

- Patients were grouped into different “recovery states” based on whether these domains had recovered (both, one but not the other, neither), and by timing: rapid recovery, delayed recovery, persistent non-recovery, or progressive worsening. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2026.1934924/full?utm_source=openai))

### Key Findings — Measured Outcomes

- Among sepsis patients in the MIMIC-IV database:

  - Those who had **coagulation recovery only** (i.e., coagulation recovered but perfusion did *not*) had significantly **higher 28-day mortality** compared to those who had *dual recovery* (both coagulation + perfusion recovered). Adjusted odds ratio (OR) = **2.54** (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.16–3.00). ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2026.1934924/full?utm_source=openai))  
  - Those with **dual non-recovery** (neither coagulation nor perfusion recovered) also had higher mortality, OR = **2.62** (95% CI 2.15–3.19), compared to dual recovery. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2026.1934924/full?utm_source=openai))  
  - Mortality ranged from **18.8%** with **rapid recovery** to **30.5%** with **progressive worsening**. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2026.1934924/full?utm_source=openai))

- The association between perfusion non-recovery and increased mortality held true even after requiring repeated measurements. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2026.1934924/full?utm_source=openai))  

### Scope & Limitations

- The findings describe risk stratification and prognosis — i.e., how likely patients are to die by day 28 depending on recovery status at 48 h — under *current care*, not the effect of any specific treatment. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2026.1934924/full?utm_source=openai))  
- The framework is observational, using existing data; it does not establish causation or test interventions. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2026.1934924/full?utm_source=openai))  
- Data are from U.S. hospital ICUs (MIMIC-IV and eICU-CRD). External validation outside U.S. settings remains to be established. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/medicine/articles/10.3389/fmed.2026.1934924/full?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Independent Corroboration & Related Studies

- A separate study titled *“Prognostic Value of 72-h Reassessment Using SOFA Score, C-Reactive Protein, and Lactate in a 72-h Landmark Cohort of Intensive Care Patients with Gram-Negative Sepsis”* evaluated reassessment at 72 hours in patients with Gram-negative bloodstream infections. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13515829/?utm_source=openai))  
  - Included 422 patients, of whom **31.8% died within 28 days**. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13515829/?utm_source=openai))  
  - Key independent predictors of mortality in that model included septic shock at baseline, the 72-h SOFA score, 72-h lactate level, and 72-h CRP. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13515829/?utm_source=openai))  
  - The 72-h model’s discrimination (AUC = 0.867) was significantly better than the baseline model (AUC = 0.799) for mortality between the 72-h landmark and day 28. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13515829/?utm_source=openai))  

- Another related study in a septic shock cohort conducted in China found that **peripheral perfusion index (PPI)** at 6 and 12 hours after ICU admission was a strong predictor of 28-day mortality, with AUCs of ~0.80 and ~0.95 respectively. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11402868/?utm_source=openai))  

These studies support the concept that *early physiologic and perfusion-related reassessment* beyond admission values can meaningfully stratify risk in sepsis.

---

## Is This a Launch, Announcement, or a Completed Outcome?

- This is a **completed research outcome**: the cohort study has been published, with measured and quantified associations (mortality rates, odds ratios), not merely an announcement or pledge.  
- The evidence is **measured and quantified**, not just a plan or hypothesis.

---

## Conclusion

- The candidate headline is **accurate** in summarizing the primary finding: that **perfusion non-recovery** at 48 hours in ICU sepsis patients is associated with **higher mortality**, even when coagulation has recovered.  
- The evidence is solid, based on large observational datasets, with effect sizes quantified (for instance, ORs around 2.5 for increased death risk when perfusion does not recover).  

If desired, I can also track whether this has led to new clinical guidelines or proposed interventional trials to change ICU practice.

stories.verified_headline: Study links perfusion non-recovery to higher sepsis mortality rates
stories.verified_summary: A study published in Frontiers in Medicine found that sepsis patients with non-recovery of perfusion at 48 hours had significantly higher 28-day mortality rates. The findings are based on large observational datasets and provide quantified associations.
stories.verification_note: The study provides strong evidence linking perfusion non-recovery to increased mortality in sepsis patients, with clear measured outcomes and independent corroboration from related studies.
